newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends steady despite RBI dlr purchases.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends steady despite RBI dlr purchases.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended steady at 35.7150/7200 against the dollar on Wednesday after touching an intraday low of 35.73 on Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervention, dealers said.
"This is now becoming a pattern," said a bank dealer, referring to the rupee gaining by the end of the day.
He said many banks did not want to buy dollars above the 35.72 level as they realised the rupee would rise to this level by day's end on the back of plentiful dollar supplies.
The rupee saw a high of 35.7150 and a low of 35.7350 on Wednesday, but most of the day's deals were at 35.725/7300.
RBI bought spot dollars in the morning session, hitting a handful of major banks at 35.7250 and stepping up the price to 35.7350, dealers said.

"He is unpredictable as ever," said a dealer referring to the central bank. "If you offered him more at the same price, he wouldn't buy." In any case, RBI's purchases had little impact on the spot rate, dealers said.
"As soon as they step in, the rupee dips and it revives as soon as they stop intervention," a dealer said.
The afternoon session saw large dollars sales, dealers said.
A major foreign bank which usually sells on behalf of foreign institutional investors (FIIs) was a major seller.
A leading Indian petrochemicals and textiles firm was also selling dollars on Wednesday, dealers said.
Forward premiums opened up in the morning. July, December, October and September dollars were active, dealers said.
"Some banks which received yesterday were cutting losses today," said a dealer. Many banks including Bank of India were selling forward dollars in the afternoon session.
The RBI made enquiries, raising expectations of intervention, but when it did not materialise, premiums began to fall, but the premiums closed higher than the morning levels.
The six month annualised premium closed at 5.04 percent, up from the previous close of 4.81 percent, dealers said.
